analysis.investment_thesis: Granules India fails both legs of the Magic Formula — Earnings Yield of ~5.5% (EBIT ₹948 Cr / EV ~₹17,237 Cr) is far below the 12% threshold, and ROCE of 15.1% falls short of the 20%+ required for a "good business." With revenue flat for three straight years and capex absorbing 62% of EBITDA, there is no compelling case to own it at current prices.
key_strengths: Long-term revenue CAGR of 14.2% (9Y) and net profit CAGR of 16.9% show the core franchise can compound over full cycles.
Diversified product mix across APIs, PFIs, and finished dosages with broad therapeutic coverage provides stability.
OCF positive all 5 of the last 5 years — not a cash-burning story, just a capital-intensive one.
key_risks: Revenue has been flat for 3 years (₹4,512 → ₹4,506 → ₹4,482 Cr), suggesting growth has stalled.
Finance costs surged from ₹26 Cr (2021) to ₹103 Cr (2025) as borrowings climbed to ₹1,807 Cr — rising debt is compressing returns.
Capex intensity is very high: ₹572 Cr capex vs ₹925 Cr EBITDA in FY25 (62%), with CWIP jumping to ₹702 Cr — FCF is thin and lumpy (FY24: just ₹61 Cr).
red_flags: Earnings Yield ~5.5% — less than half of Greenblatt's 12% minimum; stock is not cheap.
ROCE 15.1% and ROE 13.9% — both below the 20% Magic Formula threshold for a quality business.
Three consecutive years of flat revenue signals a demand ceiling or pricing pressure in key products like paracetamol/metformin.
Borrowings grew 64% from FY22 to FY25 (₹1,106 Cr → ₹1,807 Cr) while earnings barely moved.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Granules: EBIT (Operating Income) is ₹948 Cr for FY25. Enterprise Value = Market Cap ₹16,248 Cr + Net Debt (₹1,455 Cr − ₹466 Cr cash) = ~₹17,237 Cr. Earnings Yield = 948/17,237 = **5.5%** — well below the 12% floor I want to see. Return on Capital (proxied by ROCE) is 15.1%, also below my 20% minimum. Both legs of the screen fail simultaneously, which is the clearest possible signal to pass.

The business itself is not broken — a 14%+ revenue CAGR over nine years and consistent OCF generation are respectable. But the last three years show zero top-line growth, rising interest costs (4x in four years), and a capex cycle that consumed ₹572 Cr in FY25 against only ₹867 Cr of operating cash flow. That leaves negligible margin for error. At 29.9x trailing P/E and EV/EBITDA of 16.6x, the market is pricing in a growth reacceleration that hasn't materialized yet. Until revenue resumes compounding AND ROCE sustainably crosses 20%, Granules does not belong in a Magic Formula portfolio.
